content.text: : respiratory droplets, contact w/ contaminated surface
: small red spots w/ white centers on oral mucosa
for young/severely malnourished children; boosts immune response; ↓ risk of complications & death
*can suppress immune system for 6wks → otitis media, bacterial pneumonia
: type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity reaction to a pyrogenic strain (erythrogenic toxin A, B, C)
Flushed face w/ circumoral pallor & strawberry tongue
seen at pressure points, axillary, antecubital, abdominal, or inguinal areas
Penicillin G or VK first line
spreads much more rapidly than measles, does not darken/coalesce
: pinpoint red macules & petechiae on soft palate & uvula
– infects & destroys reticulocytes, leading to a ↓ or transient halt in erythropoiesis
– child appears well during febrile phase;
only viral exanthem that starts on the trunk
